references.text: God's word to Rebekah that the older shall serve the younger is a fundamental pattern repeated when Israel consciously prefers the younger Ephraim over the older Manasseh.
Isaac blesses Jacob with words suggesting that the younger (Jacob) will be preferred over the older (Esau), which mirrors how Israel (Jacob) prefers the younger Ephraim over the older Manasseh.
Joseph placed his sons so that Manasseh (the firstborn) would stand at Jacob's right hand, but Jacob deliberately crossed his hands to place his right hand on the younger Ephraim.
Joseph tries to correct his father when he crosses his hands, but Israel insists that the younger brother, Ephraim, shall be greater than Manasseh, emphasizing the action in verse 14.
Jesus laid His hands on the children and blessed them, which may recall how Israel blessed his grandchildren by laying hands on them.
By faith Jacob blessed each of Joseph's sons and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff—a direct reference to the event in Genesis 48.
Verse 20 is the direct theological conclusion of the hand-crossing in verse 14.
Prophetic confirmation that Ephraim retains the status of 'firstborn' given in Genesis 48.
